strengths: The paper provides a strong theoretical bridge between local self-supervised learning (local-SSL) and global backpropagation (global BP-SSL), proving exact equivalence under specific conditions (deep linear networks with orthonormal weights).

The theoretical insights are directly translated into practical, well-motivated algorithmic improvements: direct feedback (DFB) to handle dimensionality reduction across layers, and 2D spatial dependence for convolutional architectures.

The empirical results are outstanding, setting a new state-of-the-art for local-SSL on CIFAR-10, STL-10, and Tiny ImageNet, and remarkably closing the performance gap with comparable global BP-SSL baselines.

The paper is highly thorough, including comprehensive ablation studies, comparisons with other bio-plausible alternatives (such as Directed Feedback Alignment and Predictive Coding), and clear, illustrative figures.
weaknesses: The exact mathematical equivalence (Theorem 3.1 and 3.3) is restricted to deep linear networks. The transition to non-linear networks with ReLU is handled purely empirically, and a theoretical characterization of how non-linearities affect the approximation is lacking.

The assumption of orthonormal weight matrices is quite strong and typically not satisfied in standard deep networks. Although the authors analyze the impact of removing this condition, it remains a limitation of the theoretical foundation.

The evaluation is limited to relatively small datasets (CIFAR-10, STL-10, Tiny ImageNet) and custom VGG-like convolutional architectures. It remains unclear how well these local-SSL rules scale to larger datasets (e.g., ImageNet-1k) or modern architectures like ResNets and Vision Transformers.

The biological plausibility of CLAPP++DFB can be questioned, as sending direct feedback from the final layer ($z^L$) to all early intermediate layers requires long-range pathways that bypass the cortical hierarchy, which is structurally demanding.

strengths: Strong Theoretical Grounding: Establishing a formal mathematical connection between local-SSL and global BP-SSL in deep linear networks is highly elegant. Theorem 3.1 provides a beautiful, clean insight that weight orthonormality and learnable feedback matrices lead to exact equivalence of updates.

Principled, Theory-Guided Design: Rather than introducing ad-hoc modifications, the authors systematically use their theoretical insights (such as the impact of shrinking dimensions in Theorem 3.3 and the structured 2D spatial dependencies in CNNs) to design CLAPP++ and CLAPP++DFB.

Outstanding Empirical Performance: The proposed local-SSL algorithms achieve state-of-the-art results for local learning rules on CIFAR-10, STL-10, and Tiny ImageNet. Crucially, they close the notorious performance gap, matching or nearly matching the performance of end-to-end backpropagation (BP-SSL).

Excellent Writing and Structure: The paper is exceptionally clear, with intuitive figures (such as the conceptual overview in Figure 1 and spatial dependencies in Figure 4) and well-structured, rigorous proofs in the appendix.

Value to Biologically Plausible Deep Learning: The extensive analysis of why other frameworks (like Predictive Coding and DFA) fail or underperform on self-supervised objectives provides highly valuable negative results and constructive insights for the neuro-AI community.
weaknesses: Linearity Constraints in Theory: While the empirical results carry over well to non-linear ReLU MLPs and ConvNets, the theoretical equivalence proofs (Theorems 3.1 and 3.3) rely heavily on linear networks. Any discussion or step towards extending these approximations to non-linear networks would further strengthen the work.

Discussion of Feedback Weight Overhead: Although the paper notes that CLAPP++DFB reduces the memory footprint of storing activations compared to standard BP, training and storing the separate feedback projection matrices $B^l$ incurs computational and memory overhead. A quantitative analysis of this trade-off (FLOPs/parameters) would make the practical utility clearer.

Scale of Datasets: Although STL-10 and Tiny ImageNet are standard and challenging benchmarks for biologically plausible learning, the paper does not demonstrate how well these local-SSL rules scale to larger datasets (e.g., ImageNet-1k) or modern architectures like ResNets and ViTs, which are standard in global SSL.

Pragmatic Orthonormality: The theory relies on weight matrices being orthonormal or semi-orthonormal. In practice, standard uniform initialization and standard training are used without explicit orthonormality constraints. It would be helpful to discuss why the system remains close to the theoretical optimum even when this assumption is relaxed during training.

strengths: Provides a solid and elegant theoretical link (Theorem 3.1) showing the exact equivalence between local-SSL and global BP-SSL updates in deep linear networks with orthonormal weight matrices.

Successfully translates theoretical insights into practical, bio-plausible algorithmic improvements: Direct Feedback (DFB) for shrinking layer dimensions and 2D Spatial Dependence for convolutional architectures.

Achieves outstanding empirical performance on CIFAR-10, STL-10, and Tiny ImageNet, bridging the long-standing performance gap between local learning and backpropagation, and achieving new state-of-the-art results for local-SSL.

Well-written manuscript with extensive, clear appendices that include detailed mathematical proofs, training details, and comparisons with alternative bio-plausible methods like Predictive Coding and DFA.
weaknesses: The computational and memory overhead introduced by the spatially dependent feedback projections ($B^l$) is not thoroughly quantified compared to standard global backpropagation.

The theoretical framework is focused on contrastive loss types; how well these insights extend to non-contrastive self-supervised learning methods (e.g., Barlow Twins, VICReg) remains less explored theoretically.
The experiments are limited to VGG-like architectures on relatively small/medium datasets. Scaling to deeper networks (like ResNets) or larger datasets (like full ImageNet) is not demonstrated.

strengths: Provides a solid theoretical foundation linking local self-supervised learning (local-SSL) and global backpropagation (BP-SSL) through deep linear networks, establishing exact equivalence under specific conditions (orthonormal weights, convex loss).

Proposes a highly effective and principled modification for CNNs by introducing 2D spatial dependence in the local feedback projections (CLAPP++), which resolves a major mismatch in spatial gradient sharing between local and global learning.

The proposed method (CLAPP++ and its variants) achieves state-of-the-art results for local unsupervised learning across multiple benchmarks (CIFAR-10, STL-10, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet), virtually closing the performance gap with end-to-end backpropagation on several of these datasets.

Strong empirical analysis, including extensive control experiments, ablation studies, and comparisons to other biologically plausible credit assignment methods like Predictive Coding and Directed Feedback Alignment (DFA).
weaknesses: The theoretical guarantees (Theorems 3.1 and 3.3) rely on highly restrictive assumptions, such as linear activation functions, exact orthonormality/semi-orthonormality of weight matrices, and batch size of one. The extension to deep non-linear networks remains mostly empirical.

While the paper highlights the VRAM savings of local-SSL, the actual training was implemented using PyTorch's stop-gradient operations (Algorithm 3), which does not natively realize these memory savings. Realizing these benefits in practice would require specialized software pipelines or custom hardware.

The experiments are limited to VGG-like architectures. Modern self-supervised learning is dominated by ResNets and Vision Transformers (ViTs). It remains unclear how the proposed local learning rules would scale to residual connections or self-attention mechanisms.

strengths: The paper provides a strong theoretical bridge between local self-supervised learning (local-SSL) and global backpropagation (global BP-SSL) by deriving exact equivalence conditions in deep linear networks.

The theoretical insights are directly translated into concrete algorithmic improvements: introducing direct feedback for shrinking dimensions (DFB) and 2D spatial dependence for convolutional architectures.

The empirical results are highly compelling, showing that CLAPP++ and CLAPP++DFB match or closely approach the performance of global BP-SSL on CIFAR-10, STL-10, and TinyImageNet, setting a new state-of-the-art for local-SSL.
The work demonstrates valuable practical engineering benefits, specifically showing a 38% to 60% reduction in peak activation VRAM requirements.
The manuscript is clearly written, well-structured, and includes comprehensive proofs and control experiments (comparing with DFA and predictive coding) in the appendix.
weaknesses: The theoretical equivalence theorems rely heavily on the assumption of deep linear networks and orthonormal weights. Although numerical results show the trends hold in non-linear networks, the theory does not fully cover the non-linear case.

The evaluation is restricted to VGG-style architectures. Mainstream self-supervised learning relies heavily on residual networks (ResNets) or Vision Transformers (ViTs); scaling these local learning rules to such architectures remains an open challenge.

The reported VRAM savings are theoretical estimates. In practice, the authors used a stop-gradient implementation (Algorithm 3) rather than a custom sequential layer-by-layer execution engine, meaning the actual memory benefits were not fully demonstrated in training.

strengths: Provides a unifying theoretical framework that elegantly maps several distinct local self-supervised learning (local-SSL) algorithms (CLAPP, Forward-Forward, SCFF, PhyLL) to a common mathematical formulation.

Derives rigorous proofs showing that local-SSL can achieve identical weight updates to global BP-SSL in deep linear networks under orthonormal weights, and demonstrates how direct top-down feedback improves alignment as dimensionality shrinks.

Proposes a novel 2D spatially dependent local-SSL formulation for convolutional neural networks, addressing a major gap in how local learning rules handle spatial dimensions and proving its necessity for gradient matching.
Demonstrates strong empirical performance, setting a new state-of-the-art for local learning and successfully closing the gap to global BP-SSL on CIFAR-10, STL-10, and Tiny ImageNet.

Analyzes practical benefits, showing a potential 38% to 60% reduction in peak VRAM consumption compared to standard backpropagation, which is highly relevant for memory-constrained and biological hardware.
weaknesses: A significant performance gap of ~11-12% still remains on ImageNet (e.g., 44.16% for CLAPP++DFB vs. 55.19% for BP-InfoNCE), suggesting that the proposed local-SSL updates still struggle to scale fully to complex, high-resolution datasets.

The core theoretical equivalence relies on highly idealized conditions (linearity, orthonormality, constant layer width) that do not hold in modern architectures. Although the authors provide robust empirical relaxations, the theoretical gap for non-linear networks remains unbridged.

The reported memory savings are estimated based on ideal sequential algorithms (Algorithms 1 & 2), whereas the actual benchmark models are trained using PyTorch's stop-gradient mechanism (Algorithm 3), which does not yield actual memory savings out of the box without specialized custom training pipelines.
